area: delivery: delivery code only, emergency overrides, returned food, strikes and ban appeals
summary:
After the build, a delivery completes in one way only: someone enters the customer's 4-digit hand-over code. The rider enters it in the rider app (POST /rider/jobs/:id/deliver), or staff type it for a rider without the app (POST /trustops/orders/:id/verify-otp). Both paths go through dispatch/service.ts markDelivered → updateOrderStatus → completeOrder, so the ledger, the fiscal document (one per order, through the outbox), loyalty and rollups behave as they do today. The managers-only staff "Delivered" override is removed everywhere: POST /dispatch/orders/:id/delivered, the staffClose branch in markDelivered, and the buttons on admin /dispatch, admin /riders and the tablet Dispatch screen. The admin/management support read of the code (GET /trustops/orders/:id/otp, DELIVERY_OTP_READERS) is also removed, because a manager who can read the code can deliver without the customer.

A new Operations section, "Emergency overrides", gets a new module id `emergency_overrides`. By default it goes to management (RGM), boh_management (chef) and fnb_manager, and to admin, which always has every module. It has an admin page at /emergency-overrides and a tablet tab. It lists the operator's company's delivery orders that are on the road: stage, rider, cash to collect, whether the code has locked, and any "problem at the door" the rider reported. It also shows a 14-day log of overrides. There are two actions:

(a) **Send code to rider.** The manager gives a reason. Once per order (claimed on Order.handoverReroutedAt), after the rider has the bag or when the rider is not on the app, the code is rotated, the attempt counter is snapshotted and reset, and the new code goes by WhatsApp to the rider's own phone. The rider app (Expo and servd.pk/rider) shows the job as "code sent to you by a manager", shows the code as a fallback in case WhatsApp failed, and the rider still closes the delivery by entering it after taking any cash. The order is then pinned to that rider: reassign and unassign are refused. The step is written to RiderJobEvent 'code_rerouted' with actorId, audited in the order's company, and raises a high 'delivery_code_rerouted' exception. The customer tracker hides the code and says the rider has it.

(b) **Food came back.** Only for an undelivered 'ready' delivery order that has a rider. It cancels through the one cancelOrder path, with a new in-transaction hook. Inside that one transaction:
- Every live line is booked as waste through inventory/voidWaste.ts, using reason 'returned_undelivered' (WasteLog entries, plus Dr 5040 / Cr 1210 in the order's company keyed pos.void_waste:<lineId>).
- The stock is not put back on the shelf.
- The pending COD cash row becomes 'failed'.
- Order.returnedAt and returnCause are stamped and a 'returned' job event is written.
- Pre-bills become cancelled.

No fiscal document is created, because the order never completed. A strike is recorded only when the cause is 'refused' (the customer refused or would not pay). The old POST /orders/:id/refused-at-door is removed: this replaces it. The rider can report "customer can't get the code" or "customer refused / won't pay" from the app. That writes a 'door_problem' event and an exception for the managers; the rider never decides the outcome.

**Strikes and bans become per company.** CustomerStrike gets a tenantId (resolved from the source order or reservation, or the active company for a manual CRM strike). maybePromoteToBan counts only that company's active strikes and raises a CustomerBan with that company's tenantId. The existing column is finally written, and a partial unique index allows one active auto-ban per company and customer. Bans are matched on the customer, their known email and their phone. assertNotBannedAtCompany/banCompanies read the column first and fall back to the old attribution only where the column is NULL.

**Customers who are blocked.** Login and signup stay platform-wide and are never refused. GET /storefront/account/blocks tells the storefront, the mobile app and the brand hosts where the account is blocked, and the BANNED error at checkout carries {banId, companyName, appeal}. The customer sees a clear message and a "Ask the help desk to review" form. WhatsApp ordering answers BANNED with "reply APPEAL". An appeal is an OrderComplaint of kind 'ban_appeal' on a brand of the ban's company, in that company's Complaints queue. One open appeal per ban is enforced by a partial unique index. A manager can:
- lift the block, through the existing POST /crm/bans/:id/lift, now also open to the complaints module and resolving the appeal;
- release only the phone or email, through a new POST /crm/bans/:id/release-contact, for recycled numbers;
- keep the block, through PATCH /complaints/:id.

The customer is told the outcome by message.

**COD.** Delivered COD (the code was given) is cash held by the rider. The pay-in list GET /pos/cod-due shows each row as with rider / overdue / owed by rider. A new per-company worker flags COD not paid in after 12 h ('cod_cash_overdue'). A rider going off shift sees the cash they hold. Finance books unpaid COD only on purpose: POST /reconciliation/cod/:paymentId/rider-debt posts Dr 1351 Rider Cash Receivable (COD) / Cr 1010 (H5 default 'rider'), in the order's company, keyed cod.rider_debt:<paymentId>, inside the order lock. When the rider later hands the cash in at the till ("Take cash" → settlePayment), the same transaction reverses that entry before the normal shift close moves 1010 to 1015. The cod_unpaid customer strike and its route POST /orders/:id/cod-unpaid are removed: under the code-only rule a delivered order means the customer handed over the cash. The sales-by-tender report splits COD into paid in / with rider / owed by rider.

schema_delta:
ONE migration, e.g. 20261013160000_delivery_code_only_overrides:

model Order (add):
  // Emergency override (a), owner 2026-10-13: the hand-over code sent to the RIDER. One per order (conditional claim on null).
  handoverReroutedAt      DateTime?
  handoverRerouteRiderId  String?   // rider who received it; assignRider/takeRiderOff refuse another rider while set and undelivered
  handoverRerouteAttempts Int?      // deliveryOtpAttempts at the reroute (attempts reset to 0; riderScoring reads this)
  // Emergency override (b): food the rider brought back, logged as waste
  returnedAt              DateTime?
  returnCause             String?   // 'refused' | 'unreachable' | 'other'

model Payment (add; per-ticket, no money columns):
  // H5 default 'rider': delivered COD booked by finance as owed by the rider (Dr 1351 / Cr 1010)
  codRiderDebtAt      DateTime?
  codRiderDebtById    String?
  codRiderDebtEntryId String?

enum RiderJobEventType (add): code_rerouted, door_problem, returned
model RiderJobEvent (add): actorId String?  // staff user behind an override event; null for rider / system steps

model CustomerStrike (add):
  tenantId String?   // the company whose incident it is (order/reservation brand's company, or the active company for a manual strike); NULL only for legacy unattributable rows
  @@index([tenantId, customerId])

model CustomerBan: no Prisma field change (tenantId already exists, now always written); comment updated.

model OrderComplaint (add):
  kind         String  @default("complaint")  // 'complaint' | 'ban_appeal'
  banId        String?                         // ban_appeal: the CustomerBan appealed (same company as conceptId's)
  contactPhone String?                         // from the session / WhatsApp sender, never client-supplied
  @@index([banId])
  @@index([kind, status])

SQL-only (same migration):
  ALTER TYPE "RiderJobEventType" ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'code_rerouted'; … 'door_problem'; … 'returned';
  -- backfills BEFORE the unique indexes (see data_migration)
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "customer_bans_one_active_auto_per_company" ON "customer_bans"("tenantId","customerId") WHERE "liftedAt" IS NULL AND "bannedById" IS NULL AND "customerId" IS NOT NULL AND "tenantId" IS NOT NULL;
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "order_complaints_one_open_appeal_per_ban" ON "order_complaints"("banId") WHERE "kind" = 'ban_appeal' AND "status" IN ('open','in_progress');
(Neither partial unique is declared in schema.prisma; comment it there like the tip-pool indexes.) No RLS change: all new columns are on tables that are already scoped.
chart_accounts: 1351 Rider Cash Receivable (COD) — asset — NOT required (added to every company by ensureChartOfAccounts at boot; the rider-debt posting refuses, and nothing else needs it, if it is missing). Description: 'Delivered cash-on-delivery money a rider has not handed in (H5); cleared when the rider pays it in at the till'
postings: Food returned (waste): Dr 5040 Waste / Cr 1210 Inventory – Food, one entry per returned line through postVoidWaste. sourceType 'pos.void_waste', sourceId = orderItemId. tenantId = order.concept.tenantId. Dated now (the return). Runs inside transitionOrder's cancel transaction under lockOrderForStock. Idempotent on the journal key and the depletion row's voidWasted[lineId] marker. A refusal (PERIOD_LOCKED, ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND) leaves the cancel and the waste logs standing; it is flagged after commit with flagPostingFailed (sourceType 'pos.void_waste', metadata.wasteLogIds), and the existing REPOSTER re-posts it (its filter is widened to reason IN VOID_WASTE_REASONS)

Food returned — no other entries: the order never completed, so there is no order.complete, no fiscal document and no COGS. postCancelledTicketUnwind finds nothing to undo. The wallet / gift card / points restore through the existing postRefundOrFlag path. The COD cash row becomes 'failed' with no posting (nothing was booked for it)

COD owed by rider (H5 def 'rider'): Dr 1351 Rider Cash Receivable / Cr 1010 Cash on Hand, amount = payment.amountCents, conceptId on both lines, memo names the order ref, the full order id and the rider (and the provider company for a fleet rider). sourceType 'cod.rider_debt', sourceId = paymentId. tenantId = order.concept.tenantId. Dated now. Inside $transaction with lockOrderTx and the claim on Payment.codRiderDebtAt IS NULL. Preconditions: cash, pending, amount>0, source≠pos, status completed, delivered with the code (deliveryOtpVerifiedAt not null), rider on the order, and 'order.complete:<orderId>' entry present in that company. A refusal fails the whole request (atomic, no flag). A replay is a no-op

COD recovered at the till: in settlePayment's transaction, after the pending→paid claim, if Payment.codRiderDebtEntryId is set, reverseJournalEntry(tenantId, 'cod.rider_debt', paymentId, 'Rider handed the cash in', {tx}) posts Dr 1010 / Cr 1351 (reference cod.rider_debt:<paymentId>:reversal). The normal shift close then posts Dr 1015 / Cr 1010 (unchanged). If the reversal is refused, the settle still stands; it is flagged with flagPostingFailed sourceType 'cod.rider_debt.reversal', entity Payment, and the new REPOSTER kind re-posts it. Idempotent on the reversal key

Rerouted delivery: no new posting. The rider's code completes the order through markDelivered → completeOrder exactly as today (order.complete, one fiscal sale document from the stored figures; nothing in the sale changes)

TODO(H30) seam: for a fleet rider of another company, 1351 stays in the order's company with the provider named; it is reclassed to a due-from-provider account once the inter-company accounts exist. TODO(H5/H15) seam: writing the rider receivable off to a loss is the bad-debt path (CEO approves) and is not built here
routes: GET /emergency-overrides/orders — requireAuth(MANAGERS) + gate emergency_overrides (GATED_PREFIXES '/emergency-overrides'). Scope: read, via the order's concept.tenantId. Returns {onTheRoad:[{orderId, ref, brand, customerName, stage, rider{id,name,fleetPartner}, cashToCollectCents, codeLocked, rerouted, doorProblem, minutesOut}], recent:[RiderJobEvent code_rerouted|returned, last 14 days, with actor, rider, reason]}. A fleet partner's rider appears only on the client company's own orders

POST /emergency-overrides/orders/:id/send-code-to-rider {reason: string 10..300} — MANAGERS + gate. The order must be in write scope (foreign → 404). Errors: 422 NOT_A_DELIVERY, 409 ALREADY_DELIVERED, 409 NOT_READY, 422 NO_RIDER, 409 NOT_PICKED_UP (app job not picked up), 409 ALREADY_REROUTED, 422 RIDER_HAS_NO_PHONE, 409 ORDER_CHANGED. → {ok, sentToRider, riderPhoneHint}. Audit 'delivery.code_rerouted' in the order's company; exception 'delivery_code_rerouted' (high)
POST /emergency-overrides/orders/:id/send-code-to-rider/resend {} — MANAGERS + gate. Resends the same code to the same rider. 409 NOT_REROUTED, 409 ALREADY_DELIVERED. Rate limit 3 / 10 min per order

POST /emergency-overrides/orders/:id/food-returned {cause: 'refused'|'unreachable'|'other', reason: 5..500} — MANAGERS + gate. Write scope (foreign → 404). Errors: 422 NOT_A_DELIVERY, 409 ALREADY_DELIVERED, 409 ORDER_COMPLETED_USE_REFUND, 409 ORDER_NOT_ACTIVE, 422 NO_RIDER, 409 PAID_USE_REFUND (a paid cash/card/raast tender), 409 TERMINAL_CHARGE_ACTIVE. → {ok, wasteCostCents, wasteLogIds, codVoidedCents, strike:{recorded,duplicate}|null}

POST /rider/jobs/:orderId/door-problem {kind: 'no_code'|'refused'|'unreachable', note?: ≤300, lat?, lng?} — rider token; own open job only (else 404); 409 NOT_PICKED_UP; deduped per order+kind for 5 min; limit 10/min per rider → {ok}. Writes a 'door_problem' event and the exception 'delivery_door_problem' in the order's company
GET /rider/jobs, GET /rider/jobs/:orderId — Job gains handover {rerouted, reroutedAt, code (only when rerouted to THIS rider, else null), whatsappSent} and doorProblem {kind, at} | null
POST /rider/shift {online:false} — response adds cashHeldCents (pending COD on this rider's delivered orders not yet paid in); a warning, never a block
REMOVED: POST /dispatch/orders/:id/delivered, POST /orders/:id/refused-at-door, POST /orders/:id/cod-unpaid, GET /trustops/orders/:id/otp
POST /trustops/orders/:id/verify-otp — unchanged guard (ALL_STAFF, shared attempt budget). The 423 message now says 'ask a manager to send the code to the rider (Emergency overrides)'
GET /pos/cod-due (CASHIERS) — each row adds riderOwes {at, byName} | null and status 'with_rider'|'overdue'|'rider_owes'
GET /reconciliation/cod?status=with_rider|overdue|rider_owes — FINANCE_TEAM + reconciliation module (existing '/reconciliation' gate); read scope via order.concept

POST /reconciliation/cod/:paymentId/rider-debt {reason: 5..500} — requireAuth('admin','owner','management','finance') + reconciliation module. The payment's order must be in write scope (foreign → 404). Errors: 422 NOT_CASH_ON_DELIVERY, 409 COD_ALREADY_PAID, 409 COD_NOT_DELIVERED_WITH_CODE, 422 NO_RIDER, 409 COD_SALE_NOT_BOOKED, 409 PERIOD_LOCKED (passthrough). A replay → 200 {alreadyBooked:true}. → {ok, entryId}

GET /storefront/account/blocks — requireCustomerAuth → {blocks:[{banId, companyName, brands:[formatted names], since, appeal:{status:'none'|'open'|'declined', at}}]}. Matches the customer's id, email and phone

POST /storefront/account/ban-appeals {banId, reason:'new_number'|'mistake'|'other', message:10..1000, conceptSlug?} — requireCustomerAuth. The ban must match this customer (else 404). Contact details come from the session. 409 APPEAL_OPEN; 429 APPEAL_TOO_SOON (declined less than 30 days ago); rate limit 3/hour per customer → 201 {appealId}
WhatsApp: on BANNED, 'Reply APPEAL to ask our help desk to review this'; the 'appeal' keyword creates an appeal for that company's ban (contactPhone = the sender). One open appeal per ban
GET /complaints?kind=ban_appeal|complaint — ALL_STAFF (now scoped with scopeTenantWhere 'read', empty scope denies); appeal rows include ban {id, reason, bannedAt, auto} + this company's strikes
PATCH /complaints/:id — MANAGERS; scopeTenantWhere 'write'; 'closed' on an appeal = block kept (customer notified)

POST /crm/bans/:id/lift — existing MANAGERS route. The gate is widened by a pattern rule to anyOf ['crm','complaints']. It now also resolves the linked open appeals in the same transaction and notifies the customer

POST /crm/bans/:id/release-contact {contact:'phone'|'email', reason} — MANAGERS + pattern gate ['crm','complaints']; only this company's ban (404). Clears that fingerprint, resolves the appeal, audited
POST /crm/strikes — writes tenantId = the active company ('create'); POST /crm/bans — writes tenantId = the active company
Checkout / booking / group order / WhatsApp: the BANNED 403 adds details {banId, companyName, appeal}

- Delete staffClose and its helpers.
- Every caller passes a verified code; stamp deliveryOtpVerifiedAt every time.

Remove POST /dispatch/orders/:id/delivered and GET /trustops/orders/:id/otp. Set DELIVERY_OTP_READERS = []. Update the verify-otp and rider 423 lock messages.

data_migration:
All steps are in the one migration. Each is re-runnable because each UPDATE only touches rows that are still NULL or unset.

1. **CustomerStrike.tenantId:**
   - from the source order: UPDATE customer_strikes s SET "tenantId"=c."tenantId" FROM orders o JOIN concepts c ON c.id=o."conceptId" WHERE s."sourceType"='order' AND s."sourceId"=o.id AND s."tenantId" IS NULL;
   - the same via reservations;
   - manual strikes (sourceType NULL) take the recordedBy user's company only when that user belongs to exactly one company (primary plus memberships); otherwise they stay NULL, a legacy row that is attributed at read time as today.
2. **CustomerBan.tenantId:**
   - staff bans with a NULL tenant take the banning user's primary tenantId (the same rule migration 20260927190000 used);
   - auto bans (bannedById NULL) take X only when every non-reversed strike of that customer has tenantId X (exactly one company);
   - auto bans whose strikes span several companies, or cannot be attributed, stay NULL. The conservative legacy reading ("applies everywhere") continues, and they remain liftable from each company's naughty list. They are listed for review in the build notes. The migration lifts no ban automatically.
3. **Partial unique indexes:** created after the backfill. They cannot collide, because maybePromoteToBan never kept two active auto-bans per customer, and no appeals exist yet.
4. **New Order / Payment / RiderJobEvent / OrderComplaint columns:** NULL or default; no backfill. OrderComplaint.kind defaults to 'complaint' for every existing row.
5. **Enum values:** ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS, safe to re-run.
6. **Module access (data only, at boot):** MODULE_GRANTS 'emergency_overrides' appends the module once to saved RoleModuleAccess rows of management, fnb_manager and boh_management (marker moduleAccess.grantsApplied). A later untick by the CEO sticks.
7. **Chart:** ensureChartOfAccounts adds 1351 to every company at boot. It only adds codes that are missing.
8. **Open orders at deploy:** none need data. Codes that were already locked are unblocked by Send code to rider, which resets the attempts. Pre-rider-app undelivered orders are closed with the customer's code through verify-otp, or returned. Existing pending COD rows show as with rider / overdue until finance books them.
assumptions: Roles: RGM = 'management', chef = 'boh_management', F&B manager = 'fnb_manager', and the CEO ('admin') always. Co-owner ('owner'), foh_management and legacy 'manager' do NOT get emergency_overrides by default; the CEO can tick them in Module Access, and the route guard is MANAGERS + module. QUESTION for owner: should a floor manager (foh_management) also have it?

Module decision: a NEW id 'emergency_overrides' in Operations (its own section, as the owner asked), not an extension of 'dispatch'/'riders'. foh and cashier hold 'dispatch', and foh_management holds both, by default. Gating overrides on those modules would hand the power to floor staff. A separate id lets Module Access grant it to exactly the three roles

Send code to rider is allowed once per order. It can be used only after the rider has the bag (or when the rider is not on the app). It ROTATES the code, so a code anyone saw earlier is dead, and resets the 5-try budget (the old count is kept for scoring). It pins the order to that rider: no reassign or unassign until it is delivered or the food comes back. QUESTION: OK that the code changes and the customer's old code stops working?
The rerouted code goes by WhatsApp to the rider's phone AND is shown in that rider's app as a fallback, so a WhatsApp outage never strands a delivery. Managers never see the code

The admin/management 'support read' of the customer's code is removed. A manager reading the code is a disguised 'Delivered' override. Staff may still type the customer's code for a rider without the app (verify-otp). QUESTION: confirm no one (not even the CEO) should be able to read a customer's code
A strike is recorded only for 'customer refused or would not pay'. 'Could not reach the customer' and 'our mistake' record no strike. QUESTION: should an unreachable customer also get a strike?

Literal '3 strikes': a refused-at-door strike always weighs 1 (the old PKR 5,000+ double weight is dropped for door refusals). Reservation no-shows still count toward the same company's 3. Manual CRM strikes keep their 1-3 severity

Strikes and bans are counted and applied per company. Customer.strikeCount / bannedAt remain 'any company' mirrors. Legacy multi-company auto-bans stay as they are (apply everywhere) until a manager reviews them

Accounts are platform-wide, so login and signup are never refused. The customer is told clearly where they are blocked, ordering and booking are refused at that company's brands, and they can appeal. QUESTION: should a blocked customer be stopped from signing in at all on that brand's own site (e.g. simmer.pk)?

The help desk is the company's Complaints queue (Marketing → Customers → Complaints; fnb_manager, foh_management, management and marketing hold 'complaints'). Lifting reuses the one CRM lift route, widened to the complaints module. Appeals pick a brand of the ban's company, because OrderComplaint is scoped through its brand
'Release this number only' handles recycled numbers by clearing the phone from the ban while the original account and email stay blocked

Returned food applies only to an undelivered 'ready' delivery order with a rider. A till delivery that was already paid (completed), or any order with a paid cash/card/Raast tender, goes back through the refund engine instead

H5 default: delivered COD that never reaches a drawer is owed by the rider and booked by finance to a new 1351 Rider Cash Receivable (COD), separate from 1350 HR loans, since riders are not on payroll. For a fleet rider of another company, 1351 is booked in the order's company with the provider named (TODO H30 due-from). Recovery is in full at the till only; instalments, payroll recovery and write-off to a loss (CEO, like bad debt) are later
The COD overdue threshold stays 12 h (existing constant), moved to one definition. A per-company setting comes later
The rider can REPORT a door problem from the app but can never cancel, return or deliver without the code. The manager logs the return when the food is back
Payment rider-debt markers are per-ticket fields (no money column added); no new company-level money column is introduced
risks: The override is a collusion path: a rider and a manager can 'deliver' without the customer. Mitigations: a mandatory reason, once per order, a high exception for every reroute, the actor on the job event, and riderScoring counting reroutes.

No escape after a reroute: if a rerouted code still locks (5 more wrong tries), the only way out is Food came back. This is mitigated by showing the code in the rider app, so it should not happen in practice.
Removing GET /trustops/orders/:id/otp and the admin/management code visibility changes support practice. No frontend caller was found, but someone may read it by hand today.

Recycled phone numbers: a new holder who signs in with the WhatsApp code lands in the OLD customer account (Customer.phone is unique). The appeal and 'release number' help, but account ownership is not solved here (pre-existing).

Pre-existing cross-company effects of Customer.bannedAt are left as they are: lib/marketingAudience.ts ('no active ban anywhere') and the loyaltyTriggers referral check treat a ban at company A as a ban everywhere. Follow-up.
Postgres enum ADD VALUE in the migration: the new values cannot be used inside the same migration transaction. Do not seed rows that use them in this migration.
COD booked to 1351 during an inter-company (fleet) delivery sits in the client company until H30 accounts exist, so the provider-side recovery is manual meanwhile.
Existing tests that used the removed routes (dispatch, riderApp, ordersReconcile, managerVoids, integrationPass1, cashControls) must be rewritten in the same change, or the full suite fails.
